place.name: Low Earth orbit, 613 km up, 28.45 degrees from the equator

orbit.source: the published orbit (about 612 km at 28.45 degrees, NASA's STS-31 pages and press kit) drawn as a circle; where over the Earth the shuttle is at each minute, the clocks of everything before the release, and the two thruster pulses are ours

hst.source: the release at 19:38 UTC on 25 April 1990 (Jonathan's Space Report no. 36; America Space says 3:37 p.m. EDT) from the arm into the same orbit; where it was over the Earth is ours

audio_note: No radio recording plays. NASA's STS-31 air-to-ground audio was not found as a clearly licensed, labelled file (3 November 2026); the words are captions.
